root_cause.text: `brcmf_chip_recognition()` in the brcmfmac Wi-Fi chip detection path failed to check whether `brcmf_chip_add_core()` returned an `ERR_PTR`, and then unconditionally dereferenced the `core` pointer via `brcmf_chip_sb_corerev()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (IS_ERR(core)) return PTR_ERR(core);` immediately after each `brcmf_chip_add_core()` call in `drivers/net/wireless/broadcom/brcm80211/brcmfmac/chip.c`, and the CVE/Smatch report explicitly says `brcmf_chip_recognition()` had possible `ERR_PTR()` dereferences at lines 1010, 1013, 1016, 1019, and 1022.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add error handling after core creation during chip recognition so failures are propagated immediately instead of using invalid core pointers.
intent_record.what: In brcmf_chip_recognition(), after each brcmf_chip_add_core() call in the SOCI_SB path, the code now checks whether the returned core pointer is an error with IS_ERR(core) and immediately returns PTR_ERR(core) if so, before calling brcmf_chip_sb_corerev(). Five such error checks were added for the CHIPCOMMON, SDIO_DEV, INTERNAL_MEM, ARM_CM3, and 80211 cores.
intent_record.how: This change prevents the function from continuing when core registration fails, avoiding use of an invalid error-encoded pointer in brcmf_chip_sb_corerev() and allowing chip recognition to fail cleanly with the underlying error code instead of proceeding with corrupted state or causing a crash.
